agent.name: Silver-Milk Team Organizational Adoption Agent
agent.specialty: Organizational readiness for an emerging-technology application at the stage asked (preparation, bounded evaluation, routine operation): eight dimensions rated from case facts with owners, failed vs. absent vs. unknown kept apart, execution gates kept separate from readiness gaps, one verdict by table with a stage ladder, actions traced to gaps, and specific requests for missing evidence (adoption decisions are handed to the Adoption Agent)

analytical_question: Assuming strategic appropriateness, can the hypothetical retailer absorb, govern, staff and sustain a bounded internal concept-board evaluation, and what organizational provisions and evidence are required before separate authorization?
general_et_finding:
EVIDENCE BASE: Supplied cards
UNIT: Text-to-image diffusion models
DEMAND [D1]: Moderate — Adapt sponsorship to probabilistic image generation.
DEMAND [D2]: Moderate — Adapt skills for prompting and assessing generated images.
DEMAND [D3]: Moderate — Adapt review and revision procedures.
DEMAND [D4]: Moderate — Adapt computing, input handling and output storage to the deployment.
DEMAND [D5]: Moderate — Adapt resource allocation to generation and review workloads.
DEMAND [D6]: Moderate — Adapt risk controls to generated content and deployment terms.
DEMAND [D7]: Moderate — Adapt change handling to a generative creative tool.
DEMAND [D8]: Moderate — Adapt accountability for operation and maintenance.
TECHNOLOGY LIMIT: Working limitation, dated 2026-11-10: generated imagery cannot be treated as guaranteed faithful representation without verification. Supplied G1 provides general generative-AI risk context, not a diffusion-specific performance measurement; no current model-level reliability evidence was supplied or inspected.
application_finding:
FIT: Partial — Generating visual alternatives supports concept exploration, but dependable product-detail fidelity requires separate review.
TASK SIDE: Creative, variable and iterative work; references and visual judgment are needed, with interdependent generation, selection and revision; frequency is unspecified; concept errors matter if carried downstream.
TECHNOLOGY SIDE: Image generation offers flexible visual variation; usability, integration, reference handling and security depend on the implementation and require evaluation.
FIT GAP: Faithful preservation of specific product details.
APPLICATION ADDS: D3 — Separate speculative concept imagery from representations accepted as accurate product depictions.
UPSTREAM READ: case-premise — Assignment 6 conditionally favored preparing a bounded internal comparison, not immediate execution or rollout. No explicit DEFER GATE or POSTURE GATE was supplied. This inherited judgment does not establish organizational readiness.
organization_specific_finding:
PREMISE: Adoption is assumed strategically appropriate for this finding; adoption decisions belong to the Adoption Agent.
UNIT OF ANALYSIS: Two-person marketing operation, dependent on owner authorization and tool-rights/input-use review whose accountable role is not stated.
STAGE ASKED: Bounded evaluation — preparation precedes the proposed trial-authorization decision.
D1 Leadership/sponsorship: Not ready — Owner has NOT explicitly sponsored an AI trial; no AI evaluation sponsor designated — Owner: none stated for AI evaluation.
D2 Skills/training: Insufficient evidence — Existing visual-editing experience; AI-specific competence and training unconfirmed — Owner: none stated.
D3 Workflow/process: Insufficient evidence — Manual workflow retained; fidelity review, checklist and repeatable acceptance measures unknown — Owner: none stated.
D4 Infrastructure/data: Insufficient evidence — Catalogue references exist; approved environment and input permissions not supplied — Owner: none stated.
D5 Resources/budget: Insufficient evidence — Staff-hour allocation, availability and budget unknown — Owner: none stated.
D6 Governance/risk: Insufficient evidence — Tool rights unconfirmed; application-specific review and approval authority not supplied — Owner: none stated.
D7 Culture/change: Insufficient evidence — Staff attitudes, objections and feedback arrangements unknown — Owner: none stated.
D8 Operating ownership: Not ready — No accountable pilot lead or ongoing operating owner designated — Owner: none stated.
STRENGTHS: Employees already edit visual content; owner approves existing concepts; manual boards and freelance designer remain available.
GAPS THAT COULD CAUSE FAILURE: D1 — no AI trial sponsorship; D8 — no accountable evaluation lead.
EXECUTION GATES: Separate trial authorization — store owner is the inferred decision role, requiring confirmation; tool/input-use terms must be resolved — clearing role not stated. Terms are unknown, not demonstrated unacceptable; D6 uncertainty concerns organizational authority, not the pending terms themselves.
OPERATING OWNER: None currently exists
COUNTS: Ready 0, Partially ready 0, Not ready 2, Insufficient evidence 6
READINESS VERDICT: Not ready — required D1 and D8 are Not ready.
VERDICT BASIS: Both — observed gaps determine the verdict; missing evidence leaves additional requirements unresolved.
VERDICT SENSITIVITY: All unknowns Ready: Not ready; all unknowns Not ready: Not ready.
STAGE LADDER: PREPARATION: Supported — no stated prohibition on commissioning planning or absence of planning time. BOUNDED EVALUATION: Blocked — sponsorship and accountable leadership absent. ROUTINE OPERATION: Blocked — no permanent operating owner; all eight dimensions would be required.
FAILURE LOCUS: Organization

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: COMPETING READING: Undetermined — more evidence — someone could interpret the unassigned sponsorship and lead as documentation gaps rather than actual absences.

STRONGEST CASE AGAINST: Existing owner approval, visual-editing experience and retained fallback make preparation feasible and may allow rapid organizational changes. However, the case explicitly states that AI sponsorship and accountable leadership are not designated, so treating both as merely unknown would disregard supplied facts.

DISTINGUISHING EVIDENCE: A dated owner-approved appointment record within the six-week review, specifying AI sponsorship, decision and stop authority, an accountable evaluation lead and accepted responsibilities, would establish whether these absences have been resolved.
Contrary observations: Internal-only use, no automatic publication and retained manual work limit exposure; none establishes staffing, competence or governance readiness.

Evidence gaps: No interviews, permissions, trial outcomes, cost findings or source rechecks occurred. Supplied external descriptions do not establish current tool capabilities, rights or this organization's provisions.
confidence_and_uncertainty: VERDICT CONFIDENCE: High — within the hypothetical case, explicit D1 and D8 absences determine Not ready regardless of unknowns. Dated evidence that these provisions now exist would change the assessment. Confidence about any real retailer is low because no fieldwork occurred; general technology and task-fit judgments remain provisional without inspected technical evidence.
value_opportunity_implication: Preparation could clarify whether internal concept generation warrants the organizational effort needed for a comparison. A separately authorized evaluation could examine creative usefulness, review burden and workflow effort relative to manual/designer boards. These are proposed opportunities, not observed improvements or savings; the six-week horizon establishes a readiness decision window only.
risk_governance_implication: Preparing a proposal authorizes no real-input tool use. The owner currently approves ordinary concepts, but AI-specific approval and stop authority have not been assigned. Before execution, identify the sponsor, evaluation lead, fidelity reviewer and rights/input-permission decision role; document human review, fallback and escalation responsibilities. Manual fallback is stated; its AI-specific operation and other controls are not demonstrated. Internal-only use and no auto-publication reduce exposure without certifying safety or legal compliance.
recommendation_management_implication:
READINESS VERDICT: Not ready (Bounded evaluation) — explicit sponsorship and accountable leadership are absent.
MOST CONSEQUENTIAL GAP: D8 Operating ownership — no accountable pilot lead exists to coordinate staffing and review.
MOST CONSEQUENTIAL MISSING FACTOR: D5 Resources/budget. QUESTION: What protected hours, approved budget and coverage can be assigned to the evaluation lead and reviewers without impairing ongoing marketing work?
ACTION 1 [D8]: Assign an accountable evaluation lead and record responsibility boundaries — GAP: no pilot lead designated — OWNER: store owner (inferred) — DONE WHEN: a dated appointment identifies an accepting role and its coordination responsibilities.
ACTION 2 [D1]: Establish explicit AI-evaluation sponsorship and decision/stop authority — GAP: owner has not sponsored the trial — OWNER: store owner (inferred) — DONE WHEN: dated sponsorship records identify the sponsor and authority without conflating this with trial authorization.
ACTION 3 [D5]: Establish the staffing and budget facts — GAP: protected hours, availability and budget unknown — OWNER: store owner (inferred) — DONE WHEN: a dated allocation record states hours, review coverage, backfill arrangements and approved resource limits.
NOW: Map the existing manual workflow, collect the missing readiness evidence and draft responsibilities and approval questions without using the tool on real inputs.
change_monitoring_triggers: TRIGGER [D8]: Within the six-week review, a dated completed readiness record establishes D1 and D8 as Ready and resolves every other required-dimension unknown to at least Partially ready → Ready after named conditions — remaining weaknesses or execution gates must be named; appointing a lead alone cannot produce this change.
TRIGGER [D1]: Within the six-week review, a dated complete readiness determination establishes all eight dimensions Ready and records all execution gates cleared → Ready.
No lower readiness verdict exists below Not ready; worsening facts can expand the blockers but cannot produce a lower allowed verdict.
REVIEW DATE: 2026-11-24 — proposed interim review within the six-week horizon, using 2026-11-10 as the assessment date rather than an asserted case start date.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: MORE INFO → D5 Resources/budget: Request protected hours, budget approval and coverage/backfill for evaluation coordination and fidelity review — WHY IT MATTERS: establishes whether the bounded stage can be staffed; cannot override D1/D8 blockers alone.

MORE INFO → D6 Governance/risk: Request the roles authorized to review and clear this application's tool rights, confidentiality, input use and risk conditions, with review scope and stop/escalation authority — WHY IT MATTERS: distinguishes an organizational governance provision from a pending execution gate.

MORE INFO → D3 Workflow/process: Request the application-specific review, acceptance, fallback and escalation procedure, the fidelity review owner, and evidence of any demonstration required by the owner — WHY IT MATTERS: determines whether a working evaluation process exists.

MORE INFO → D4 Infrastructure/data: Request the proposed environment, reference-input permissions, storage/access provisions and the role/process responsible for approving them — WHY IT MATTERS: determines organizational data/environment readiness while keeping selection-dependent items as gates.

MORE INFO → D2 Skills/training: Request tool-specific competence evidence, any training provision and its accountable role — WHY IT MATTERS: resolves a nonrequired bounded-stage dimension that can constrain a Ready verdict and becomes required for routine operation.

MORE INFO → D7 Culture/change: Request recorded staff concerns, willingness, feedback channels, change responsibilities and any unsanctioned-use findings — WHY IT MATTERS: resolves change readiness without inferring attitudes from aggressive adoption posture or visual-editing experience.

INTAKE MISSING: Named AI sponsor with decision/stop authority; named evaluation coordinator and permanent operator; approved environment scope and input permissions; confirmation that contracts/controls cover the actual tool; protected hours, budget and backfill; application-specific review/fallback/escalation procedure and demonstration status; governance reviewers and scope; AI-specific skills evidence and training owner; recorded objections, feedback channels and unsanctioned-use status. Stage and internal-only scope are supplied.
